Every locality is the real 2022 result, swung uniformly to match the national vote share implied by the model above: each current party's 2022 predecessor vote is scaled by a single national factor (projected share ÷ 2022 share), applied evenly everywhere and renormalized to 100% per locality — a simplification, not a forecast of local campaigning. New parties with no 2022 predecessor have no local history to swing from, so they're assumed to perform uniformly everywhere, at their national projected share. The underlying locality shapes and 2022 counts are the real, sourced results: 981 localities as real jurisdiction polygons matched by official locality code (Ministry of Interior boundaries, CBS data, and Central Elections Committee results), plus 117 West Bank settlements shown as dots since they have no polygon in that boundary layer. Altogether the map accounts for of the national vote; the remainder has no coordinate in the source data (overwhelmingly unrecognised Bedouin villages) or is overseas/military-base polling.
